label: <DEL> delimiter step in long sequences (L = 8 or 9)
explanation: Fires almost exclusively on the <DEL> delimiter step of sequences with 8 or 9 original tokens (fires on essentially every such step), and never on the delimiter for L <= 7 or on any copy-phase step. Magnitude depends on length: with roughly equal step counts, L=9 delimiters carry about 66% of activation mass and L=8 about 34%, so L=9 activations are about twice as large (top examples near 1.0 are all L=9). Token identity, first token, and which token comes next have little effect; there is a mild increase with the number of digits. Rare weak activations (about 0.05%) appear on the last original token of L=9 sequences or at t=7, e.g. 0.13-0.22 just before <DEL>.

issues: Minor factual error in the explanation: it says the feature never fires on the delimiter when L <= 7, and that the weak 0.1-0.2 activations at t=7 fall on the step before <DEL>. They don't. On the dev split, all 224 t=7 activations are L=7 delimiter steps (by-L: L=7 has 224 active; the original phase has only 86, all at t=8, L=9). On test, '(phase==1)&(L==7)' has precision 0.003 and mass recall 0.0004. So the feature does fire weakly on the L=7 delimiter, but only about 0.3% of the time, which is negligible.
The remaining misses are weak (about 0.1) activations on the last original token of L=9 sequences (t=8). They carry about 0.1% of the mass, as the explanation says.

The 69 test false positives (L=8 delimiter steps where the feature is silent) look like scattered noise. The visible cases often end in 'h', but '(phase==1)&(L==8)&(prev_tok==h)' still has precision 0.995 over 2816 steps, so a preceding 'h' is not a systematic false-positive class.

The phase and length claims check out on dev: zero copy-phase activations; active on about 99.8% of L>=8 delimiter steps; mass split 0.341 for L=8 (t=8) and 0.659 for L=9 (t=9). Test scores match the report: P 0.9996, R 0.998, F1 0.9988, mass recall 0.9995.
